description: A multiplex agent-based simulation on a social network modeling mask-wearing behavior with layer-specific peer influence, information exposure, and a government intervention starting on Day 10. Parameters are calibrated on days 0-29 and used to predict days 30-39.

parameters.state_source: train_data.csv day==0 wearing_mask, fallback agent_attributes.csv initial_mask_wearing
parameters.risk_imputation: impute missing risk_perception via subgroup Beta posterior
parameters.random_intercept: draw from N(0, sigma_u^2) if using GLMM; else set to 0

behaviors.name: update_info_exposure
behaviors.description: Simulate whether an agent receives information on a given day from exogenous campaigns and social propagation with decay.

parameters.social_info_coeff: beta_info_social (influence of neighbors' info at t-1)

behaviors.algorithm: For each agent i at day t: 1) Compute decayed info_memory_i = info_memory_i * exp(-ln(2)/H). 2) Compute neighbor_info_rate = fraction of neighbors that had received_info at day t-1 (across all layers or weighted). 3) Compute p_info_i(t) = clip(p_info_base_by_day[t] * policy_info_boost_factor + social_info_coeff * neighbor_info_rate, 0, 1). 4) Draw received_info_i(t) ~ Bernoulli(p_info_i(t)). 5) If received_info_i(t)==1, set info_memory_i = 1.

behaviors.name: compute_peer_mask_rates
behaviors.description: Compute lagged fraction of neighbors wearing masks by layer to drive social influence.

parameters.overlap_handling: do not double-count neighbors across layers when computing overall rate

behaviors.algorithm: For each agent i and layer l in {family, work_school, community}: m_i,l(t-1) = (# neighbors in layer l wearing mask at t-1) / (degree in layer l). If degree==0, set m_i,l(t-1)=0. Option A (layered logit): pass m_i,l individually to behavior model. Option B (aggregated): m_i,agg = sum_l w_l * m_i,l(t-1).

behaviors.name: adoption_persistence_decision
behaviors.description: Update agent mask state using a two-regime logistic model with peer effects, info effects, risk perception, subgroup effects, and random intercepts.
behaviors.algorithm: For agent i at day t: If wearing_mask_i(t-1)==0, compute logit p01_i(t) = a0 + u_i + a_info*received_info_i(t) + a_risk*risk_i + sum_l a_l*m_i,l(t-1) + a_FE[group_i] + a_policy*I(t>=10); set wearing_mask_i(t) ~ Bernoulli(sigmoid(p01_i(t))). If wearing_mask_i(t-1)==1, compute logit p11_i(t) = c0 + u_i + c_info*received_info_i(t) + c_risk*risk_i + sum_l c_l*m_i,l(t-1) + c_FE[group_i] + c_policy*I(t>=10); set wearing_mask_i(t) ~ Bernoulli(sigmoid(p11_i(t))).

behaviors.name: apply_policy_effects
behaviors.description: Impose intervention effects on targeted layers (e.g., workplace mandates) as logit shifts and optional direct compliance.
behaviors.algorithm: If t >= policy_start_day and agent has degree in a mandated layer: add mandate_logit_shift.{adoption|persistence} to the corresponding logits. Optionally, with probability direct_compliance_prob, force wearing_mask_i(t)=1 for that day (emulating on-site enforcement), which also feeds into neighbors' observed mask rates at t.

interactions.name: social_influence_peer_effect
interactions.description: Layer-weighted peer influence where neighbors' mask-wearing at t-1 affects agent adoption/persistence at t.
interactions.effect: Shifts adoption/persistence logits via layer-specific coefficients applied to lagged neighbor mask rates.

interactions.name: information_propagation
interactions.description: Agents receive information from exogenous campaigns and socially via neighbors' info exposure, with memory decay.
interactions.effect: Increases probability of adoption and persistence for informed agents; may have lingering effects via info_memory.

interactions.name: government_intervention
interactions.description: From Day 10, modifies info intensity and/or behavioral logits; can also impose direct compliance in targeted layers.
interactions.effect: Boosts info exposure probability and adds positive shifts to adoption/persistence logits for targeted agents.

parameters.assortativity_mixing: estimated from data; used only if synthesizing network
parameters.threshold_mapping: optional: theta_i = 1 - risk_perception_i (if using threshold variant)
parameters.p_info_daily: vector by day; boosted after policy start

calibration.lagged_variables: use t-1 for neighbors and info

steps: Load agent_attributes.csv; coerce types; derive subgroup_label = f(age_group, occupation).
Load social_network.json; normalize keys to int; symmetrize edges per layer; remove self-loops; de-duplicate overlaps for 'all'.
Attach attributes to nodes; compute degrees per layer; flag isolates.
Load train_data.csv; verify continuity per agent; fill or drop missing days per rules.
Set initial wearing_mask from train_data day==0 if available; else from agent_attributes initial_mask_wearing.
Estimate risk_perception Beta(alpha,beta); impute missing values from subgroup posterior.
Precompute lagged neighbor mask rates by layer for days 0-29 for calibration.
Calibrate behavior model (GLMM/logit) to obtain coefficients; freeze parameters for prediction.
Set policy parameters and info schedule; mark policy activation on day 10.

algorithms.SymmetrizeMultiplex: For each layer, add reciprocal edges if missing; remove self-loops and duplicates.
algorithms.LaggedNeighborRates: For each agent-day, compute fraction of neighbors wearing masks at t-1 by layer; handle zero-degree as 0.
algorithms.TwoRegimeLogisticUpdate: Separate logistic equations for adoption (0->1) and persistence (1->1) with peer, info, risk, subgroup, policy, and random intercept terms.
algorithms.InfoProcessWithDecay: Bernoulli draw with base day effect, social exposure from neighbors' info, and geometric decay memory.
algorithms.InterventionScheduler: Activate policy at configured start_day; apply info boost and logit shifts thereafter.
algorithms.NetworkSynthesisFallback: If JSON missing, generate per-layer configuration models from degree sequences with assortative rewiring; enforce even stub sums.
algorithms.Evaluation: Compute daily aggregate adoption rates; RMSE on days 30-39; Peak Adoption Rate Error and Time-to-Peak Error during intervention window.
algorithms.Sensitivity: Sweep peer coefficients, info boost, and layer weights to test robustness (optional).
